commands.command: wsl --shutdown (full WSL VM shutdown to clear all stale WSLg/RDP session state accumulated from repeated agent launch/kill cycles)
commands.summary: Confirmed via `tasklist` that msrdc.exe, wslrelay.exe, and wslhost.exe all terminated.

commands.command: (Jeremy) opened a brand-new WSL Debian terminal and ran repopact-desktop again
commands.summary: Jeremy's own words: 'yep that worked.' The clean WSLg session (with no leftover stale RAIL window registrations from the many prior agent-driven launch/kill cycles in this session) resolved the unresponsive-taskbar-icon issue.

environment.lesson: Repeatedly launching and killing a WSLg GUI app across many agent-driven wsl.exe invocations in one session can leave stale RAIL/RDP window registrations that make a live window's taskbar entry appear present (with a working thumbnail preview) but unresponsive to clicks, for both the agent's own session and the operator's real session. A full `wsl --shutdown` followed by a fresh terminal and a single launch resolves it. This is a WSLg session-hygiene issue, not an application defect.
